chapter_title: Chương 90: Các bạn đi học, tôi mở công ty

segments.title: Chương 90: Các bạn đi học, tôi mở công ty
segments.content:
The military training ended, and they returned to school by bus.

Dorm 404 still only had Chen Guiliang and Jiang Junlai.

The other two, according to the Yuanpei Program's rules, would likely be sophomores or juniors.

Because multiple grade levels had military training, the start of the school year was particularly late this year, pushed back to between September 13th and 17th (varying by department).

The day after returning to campus, while other departments were conducting freshman orientation, the Yuanpei Program was holding a course selection planning meeting.

The entire class was both excited and bewildered.

Peking University's entire, densely packed course catalog was laid out before them to choose from freely; they could even sign up for courses from the Health Science Center.

Returning from the cafeteria after lunch, Dorms 403 and 404 were buzzing with talk of course selection.

"The course catalog has given me analysis paralysis," complained Deng Chen from Dorm 403 across the hall.

Jiang Junlai asked, "Chen Guiliang, what course combination are you choosing?"

Chen Guiliang said, "It's still early, we can take our time. We still have to listen to lectures from our academic advisors and part-time mentors over the next few days. We'll just see which mentor is the most persuasive and can get us excited."

"I'm definitely not switching to the sciences in the future." As the provincial top scorer in liberal arts, Yun Fan made a bold declaration on the spot.

Back at the door of 404.

Jiang Junlai said in pleasant surprise, "The door isn't fully closed. A new roommate must have arrived."

Two new roommates had come.

One was in the dorm at that moment.

The other's bed wasn't even made. A suitcase was tossed on the empty bed, and a computer sat on the desk, but the person himself was nowhere to be seen.

"Hello, my name is Min Wenyu. I'm a sophomore in liberal arts, and I'll be choosing my major next semester." The speaker, wearing a T-shirt and with a side-part hairstyle, was slightly thin.

Chen Guiliang went over to shake his hand, "Hello, Senior Min. My name is Chen Guiliang."

Min Wenyu smiled, "I've heard so much about you. You're quite popular on the Peking University BBS."

Jiang Junlai also introduced himself and eagerly asked, "Senior Min, how did you go about choosing your courses?"

Min Wenyu said, "Let's not talk about the required courses. I also chose Principles of Economics, Behavioral Economics, Social Statistics, Fieldwork and Survey Methods, History of Western Art, Basic Physics Experiments, Introduction to Archeology, and so on."

"Introduction to Archeology?" Jiang Junlai was surprised.

Min Wenyu said, "That class is very popular. I went to the computer lab at midnight and waited by a computer all night. The moment online course registration opened, I had to be lightning fast to grab a spot!"

Jiang Junlai looked at Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang also couldn't figure out why an Introduction to Archeology class would be so highly sought after.

"We can register for classes online?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Min Wenyu nodded, "There's a course selection website for the university, though the page is very crude and simple. The registration function opens at six in the morning on the first day of each semester."

Chen Guiliang pointed at the suitcase on the empty bed, "What's this senior's name?"

"Guo Feng, a junior. He's a legend."

Min Wenyu chuckled, "It's like he's intentionally choosing courses at random. His focus is on biology, but he's also taken ecology, human geography, sociology, ancient architecture, history, statistics, computer science, and so on."

"Can he even graduate like that?" Jiang Junlai was a bit baffled.

Min Wenyu said, "He's almost got enough credits. Once his thesis is approved, he can graduate. But this guy... how should I put it, he's very lost. He himself doesn't know what he should be doing."

Chen Guiliang was delighted. He finally had an eccentric roommate.

The Yuanpei Program never lacked for eccentrics.

There was even one who got in through the Chemistry Olympiad, then in his senior year, begged his advisor for a letter of recommendation to intern on a film set as a photography assistant, then became a director and shot a short film, and then went abroad to study finance at a prestigious university.

There was also a provincial liberal arts top scorer who insisted on transferring to Peking University's mathematics department while also minoring in history and philosophy...

The "one-person graduation photo" for paleontology that went viral online in later years was also of a Yuanpei Program student. She was the only student in the entire major, with a curriculum spanning biology, geology, environmental sciences, and other fields, taught directly one-on-one by academicians and professors. (This major perennially had only one student; any year it managed to enroll two was cause for celebration.)

His phone rang. It was Bian Guanyue.

"I finished my military training and I'm back at school. What about you?" Bian Guanyue said.

Lying on his bed, Chen Guiliang said, "I got back yesterday."

Bian Guanyue said, "Wu Meng chatted with me on QQ. She's in Dorm 105 in Building 36. I also gave her your current phone number. She said she wants to ask you to eat at the cafeteria together sometime. Is your place far from hers?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Not far, I live right upstairs from her."

"You're lying again!" Bian Guanyue's tone was a bit playful and chiding.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm really not lying. I'm in 404 in Building 36. It's a co-ed dorm."

"So you really are close..." Bian Guanyue was speechless.

Then, Bian Guanyue started talking about her five roommates. She said four of them were great, but one was extremely dramatic, a total basket case.

Chen Guiliang comforted her for a bit, "Let's all get together during the National Day holiday, and call Li Rui too."

"Okay!" Bian Guanyue said happily.

They chatted for over half an hour before hanging up.

"Girlfriend?" Jiang Junlai was like a curious child.

Chen Guiliang gave an ambiguous reply, "Mhm."

Min Wenyu pointed to a row of books on the history of the Ming Dynasty, "Did you bring these?"

"Just for some research," Chen Guiliang said.

"Right, I brought something good too."

Chen Guiliang ran to Dorm 403 and knocked on the door, "Yun Fan, Deng Chen, come play cards!"

"Play what?"

At the mention of cards, the provincial and city top scorers from across the hall immediately perked up.

Chen Guiliang took out a *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* set made from playing cards from his drawer and said to Min Wenyu, "It's a card game I made myself. Senior Min, want to join a round?"

Min Wenyu came over for a look. In the middle of each card was a correction label, with various things written on it in pen.

There were also crudely drawn diagrams of trigrams, peaches, an eight-foot serpent spear, and so on.

The general cards were drawn even more abstractly. Diaochan, for example, was just a stick figure. The long hair indicated she was female, and there was a note beside her: "I am Diaochan. I am very pretty."

"Cao Cao. Treachery: When you take damage, you may obtain the card that dealt this damage. Escort: Lord's Skill, when you need..."

Jiang Junlai, Yun Fan, and Deng Chen were also looking at a few cards each.

"Looks pretty fun."

"Let's play a round and see."

"..."

They were all smart people and quickly figured out how to play.

They were unfamiliar during the first two or three games, making all sorts of random moves. But they gradually got the hang of it, almost turning *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* into a game of *Werewolf*.

You shouldn't assume these top scorers and first-prize winners only knew how to study; they could be just as wild when it came to having fun. This was especially true for Senior Min, who had chosen a ton of courses. Lacking recreational activities, he was instantly hooked on *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*.

They played until evening, only stopping when their stomachs started to grumble.

On the way to the cafeteria, Min Wenyu was still saying, "No one's allowed to run off after dinner, we're continuing the game!"

Yun Fan asked, "Are there ways to play with more people?"

"There's an eight-player mode," Chen Guiliang said.

Min Wenyu said, "Then let's play the eight-player mode. We'll find three more people."

Just as they got downstairs, Wu Meng called, "Haha, Great Hero Chen, I can't believe you live in the same building as me. This is my new phone number. I bought it with my scholarship money."

"Come out for dinner. I'm right at the entrance of the dorm building," Chen Guiliang said.

"Wait for me."

In less than two minutes, four girls from the Chinese department stormed over.

Their looks were all rather average, and they didn't know how to dress up. Wu Meng was surprisingly the prettiest one in their dorm.

Chen Guiliang was a looks-supremacist; his heart was as still as water towards these four girls.

"Hello, Great Hero Chen!"

"Haha, I didn't expect you to be living in Building 36."

"You have to sign my copy when you publish a book someday."

"..."

The girls chattered away. Even if they hadn't known about Chen Guiliang before, Wu Meng had been evangelizing to them about him for days.

Two of the girls even followed suit and called him "Great Hero Chen."

While eating in the cafeteria, the male and female students from rice-growing regions started complaining again that the rice at Cafeteria Number One was too hard.

Chen Guiliang poured the free seaweed and egg drop soup into his rice to let it soak for a bit, lamenting, "My stomach isn't great. I was born to eat soft rice."

A particularly bold girl from the Chinese department named Xia Man joked, "Then just live off a woman. I'll do my best to become a rich lady."

"Great Hero Chen has a girlfriend. She's studying here in the capital, and her family is very rich," Wu Meng said, remembering Bian Guanyue's instructions, quickly stepping in to defend her friend from the female wolf.

Xia Man sighed, "Alas, it seems I've lost my chance. It's so hard to start a business and become a rich lady on your own."

Senior Min said with a smile, "The rice at Cafeteria Number One is hard because the cooks don't add enough water each time. you can try the other cafeterias."

Hearing this, Jiang Junlai was extremely conflicted.

In the future, should he eat the hard rice at the closest Cafeteria Number One? Or should he walk a little farther to eat soft rice?

It was a difficult decision.

Wu Meng inquired, "Can you students from the Yuanpei Program choose courses from our Chinese department?"

"You can choose any course," Senior Min helped answer. "Two of my courses are even from the Guanghua School of Management."

"You can take classes at Guanghua too?"

Another girl was stunned. It seemed they already knew how prestigious the Guanghua School was.

Min Wenyu said, "Some popular courses are very hard to get. You have to stay by a computer all night, and the spots are usually all gone within a minute or two."

Senior Min seemed to enjoy showing off, and he went on to talk about the legendary figures from previous Yuanpei Program classes, leaving the four girls from the Chinese department dumbfounded.

Wu Meng muttered, "Good thing I didn't enroll in the Yuanpei Program. You guys are too... too incredible."

After dinner, they chatted all the way back to the dorm and continued playing *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*.

They even roped in three more people from nearby dorms, starting an eight-player game right away.

Two of them were from Chen Guiliang's class.

One was named Zhao Beibei. He had delicate features; he'd probably be quite popular with perverts if he cross-dressed.

The other was Zeng Changgao, the science studies representative of their class.

After playing for a while, Chen Guiliang asked Min Wenyu, "Senior Min, are there any business secretarial firms around here?"

"What's a business secretarial firm?" Min Wenyu asked back.

Chen Guiliang said, "A company that provides services like registered address hosting, proxy accounting, and receiving legal documents."

"You could just say business registration agency. Some people in the south also call it business services," Min Wenyu played a card. "Snatch! You, there... let me take a look at your hand."

It wouldn't be until next year that the state would significantly revise the company law.

Right now, the threshold for registering a company was still high. The registered capital had to be paid in full, so many small companies used agencies.

Chen Guiliang asked, "If I want to start a company, Senior Min, do you know any reliable agencies?"

Hearing this, the several freshmen were quite surprised.

School hadn't even officially started, and Chen Guiliang was already planning to start a company?

Min Wenyu answered without thinking, "There are incubator programs in Zhongguancun. You could give it a try."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Are the incubator programs in Zhongguancun hard to apply for?"

Min Wenyu took out his phone, "I'll ask some seniors from the Guanghua School."

He played cards while making the call.

Only after he, as the spy, was eliminated did he hang up and say, "There are three types of incubators in Zhongguancun: government-run, university-run, and corporate-run."

"The most famous government-run ones are the Zhongguancun Pioneer Park and the Haidian Pioneer Park for Overseas Scholars. The requirements for the entrepreneurs and project qualifications are quite high."

"The university-run ones are more suitable for you. Both Peking University and Tsinghua have science park incubators."

"Don't worry about the corporate ones. Those are more complicated and too restrictive."

Chen Guiliang asked, "What do I need to do if I want to apply for the Zhongguancun Peking University Incubator Program?"

Min Wenyu said, "Submit your materials to the Peking University Science Park Incubator Management Office. The address is near the East Gate of PKU. You need proof of your status as a PKU student... basically, just bring your student ID and national ID card. You also need a business plan. It'd be even better if you have proof of any technological achievements."

"Is it difficult to get approved?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Min Wenyu said, "It probably won't be difficult."

"What if I just want to register a company and have a registered address hosted?" Chen Guiliang said.

Min Wenyu said with a smile, "Just for hosting a registered address, you just have to pay an annual fee of 2000 yuan. It comes with three years of free financial and tax agency services, and they'll help you get your business license too."

Chen Guiliang asked again, "If I manage to make a bit of a name for myself, are there any further preferential policies?"

Min Wenyu said, "They provide low-cost office space, with rent at a few dozen yuan per square meter per month. Some are as low as 20 yuan per square meter, though the environment is a bit poor. They also help with financial and tax services for free, and let you share some of PKU's conference rooms and lab equipment. If you do exceptionally well, they can help you apply for angel investment and for government science and technology funds. If you're really, really amazing, they might even help you apply for the Torch Program."

Chen Guiliang couldn't help but feel moved: Peking and Tsinghua really are amazing, what a great place to start a business.

"What kind of company are you going to start?" Jiang Junlai asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Not sure yet."

The next morning, Chen Guiliang woke up early.

He took out a pen and paper and wrote down two key phrases: "*Legends of the Three Kingdoms*" and "*Xiaonei Wang*."

*Legends of the Three Kingdoms* would bring in money quickly, so it had to be done first.

If *Xiaonei Wang* was done well, it could attract huge investments, but that wouldn't happen overnight.

While the freshmen had just finished their military training and hadn't even attended their opening ceremony, Chen Guiliang was already at the Peking University Science Park Incubator Management Office on Haidian Road with his business plan in hand.

Great Hero Chen was going to start a company.

(Everyone, please help come up with a name for the company.)
